---
title: "Exercise 1: Your first pull request"
description: "Branch, commit, push and open a pull request."
---

**Goal**: add yourself to the [attendees page](attendees.qmd) through the full Git workflow: branch → edit → commit → push → pull request.

You'll create your **own file**, so nobody's change conflicts with anyone else's.

## 1. Get the latest version of `main`

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

1. In the **Git** pane, check the branch menu (top right of the pane) says `main`.
2. Select **Pull** (blue down arrow).

## Positron

1. Check the status bar (bottom left) says `main`.
2. In **Source Control**, select **...** → **Pull**.

## Terminal

```bash
git switch main
git pull
```
:::

## 2. Create a branch

Use your first name, then a slash, then `hello`, e.g. `alex/hello`. Lowercase, no spaces.

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

1. In the **Git** pane, select **New Branch** (the purple icon).
2. **Branch name**: `alex/hello`
3. Leave **Remote** as `origin` and **Sync branch with remote** ticked.
4. Select **Create**. The branch menu now shows `alex/hello`.

## Positron

1. Click `main` in the status bar.
2. Choose **Create new branch...**
3. Type `alex/hello` and press Enter. The status bar now shows `alex/hello`.

## Terminal

```bash
git switch -c alex/hello
```
:::

## 3. Add your file

1. Open `exercises/attendees/example.qmd`.
2. Save a copy as `exercises/attendees/alex.qmd` (your name, lowercase).
3. Change the `title` to your name and the `description` to a sentence about your work. Save.

The **Git** pane (RStudio) or **Source Control** view (Positron) now lists your new file as untracked (`?` or `U`).

## 4. Commit

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

1. In the **Git** pane, select **Commit**. The **Review Changes** window opens.
2. Tick **Staged** next to `exercises/attendees/alex.qmd`. The diff below shows every line as added (green).
3. **Commit message**: `Add Alex to attendees`
4. Select **Commit**, then **Close**.

## Positron

1. In **Source Control**, hover over `alex.qmd` and select **+** (Stage Changes).
2. In the message box at the top, type `Add Alex to attendees`.
3. Select **Commit**.

## Terminal

```bash
git add exercises/attendees/alex.qmd
git commit -m "Add Alex to attendees"
```
:::

## 5. Push

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

Select **Push** (green up arrow) in the **Git** pane.

## Positron

Select **Publish Branch** in **Source Control**.

## Terminal

```bash
git push -u origin alex/hello
```
:::

## 6. Open a pull request

1. Go to <https://github.com/harmonicr/acpcc_git_training>. A yellow banner says your branch had recent pushes. Select **Compare & pull request**.
2. Check the arrow reads **base: main ← compare: alex/hello**.
3. Leave the title, add a line in the description, then select **Create pull request**.
4. Scroll down. A check called **render** starts; it builds the whole site with your change. Wait for the green tick (about 3-5 minutes).

The facilitator reviews and merges the pull requests. After yours is merged, your name appears on the [attendees page](attendees.qmd) of the live site within a few minutes.

## 7. Tidy up

Switch back to `main` and pull, so your copy includes everyone's changes:

::: {.panel-tabset group="ide"}
## RStudio

Choose `main` from the branch menu in the **Git** pane, then select **Pull**.

## Positron

Click the branch name in the status bar, choose `main`, then **Sync Changes** (or **...** → **Pull**).

## Terminal

```bash
git switch main
git pull
```
:::

`exercises/attendees/` now contains everyone's files.
